key_insight: A learned patient world model could support multiple ICU planning simulations without rebuilding patient-state models for each policy question.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help health systems explore how ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity affect care demand and resource use before implementation.
method: Train a neural patient-trajectory model on longitudinal MIMIC-IV electronic health records.
Freeze the model and connect its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues.
Adapt scenario-specific mappings to simulate different operational policies.
evidence_signal: In simulation evaluations, the model matched Markov and semi-Markov comparators on aggregate occupancy and directional policy responses, while capturing a history-dependent 24-hour recovery contrast of −6.4 percentage points versus −6.7 observed.
watch_item: Simulation agreement does not establish real-world operational benefit; validation beyond MIMIC-IV and prospective evaluation remain important.
paper_title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
